Reference Number: POC-92D596C7F2-83353
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-03
Service/Procedure Denied: Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030

To the MedStar Family Choice DC Appeals Committee:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030 (lumbar laminotomy/hemilaminectomy with decompression of nerve root and excision of herniated intervertebral disc), issued on 2026-08-03 under reference number POC-92D596C7F2-83353. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity."

I want to note at the outset that MedStar Family Choice DC's public utilization-management materials state that non-pharmacy prior-authorization decisions are based on a combination of sources, including "InterQual or ASAM guidelines," "Medicare and Medicaid Guidelines," "District of Columbia regulations and contract requirements," and "MedStar Family Choice DC Managed Care Plan benefit coverage," and that "MedStar Family Choice DC's utilization management decision making is based on the medical necessity of the service and the existence of Managed Care Organization enrollment and coverage." I was not able to obtain, and this letter does not quote, any MedStar Family Choice DC medical policy document specific to CPT 63030 or lumbar decompression surgery, because I could not locate one on the plan's published medical-policy list. I am formally requesting, as this appeal is submitted, that MedStar Family Choice DC provide in writing the specific clinical criteria (InterQual or otherwise) applied to reference number POC-92D596C7F2-83353, together with an itemized list of the documentation elements considered missing, so that this appeal and any further review can respond to them precisely. MedStar Family Choice DC's own utilization-management page states that "All criteria applied in utilization management are available upon request. The request can be made independent of a specific case," and I am relying on that statement in making this request.

In the meantime, the following clinical documentation was submitted, or is available to be submitted, with the prior authorization request and directly addresses medical necessity for CPT 63030:

1. Symptom duration and chronicity: Jordan Hayes has experienced 18 months of progressive lower back pain that is unrelieved by rest.

2. Conservative treatment attempted and failed:
   - Supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, over 8 weeks (2026-04-14 to 2026-06-09), with 16 visits completed, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
   - NSAID therapy for 8 months with inadequate relief.
   - Corticosteroid injection administered 2026-04-29, which produced only 2 weeks of partial relief.

3. Objective imaging correlating with symptoms: MRI of the lumbar spine dated 2026-06-16 demonstrates an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.

4. Functional limitation: Jordan Hayes is unable to stand for more than 10 minutes and has radicular pain radiating into the right calf.

5. Corroborating physical examination findings: positive provocative testing on the affected side, with a neurologic deficit that corresponds anatomically to the level shown on imaging (L4-L5/L5 nerve root).

6. Absence of contraindications: no active infection, no untreated substance use disorder, BMI 29, non-smoker.

7. Requesting surgeon: Dr. Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery, who evaluated the patient and recommended CPT 63030 based on the above findings.

If any specific document listed above (e.g., the physical therapy discharge note, the imaging report, the injection procedure note, or the surgeon's clinical evaluation) was omitted or was not received in a form the plan considered complete, please identify precisely which document(s) are missing or insufficient so that [provider's office/practice name] can supply them without delay. I am enclosing/asking Dr. Lindqvist's office to enclose the following in support of this appeal: [PT discharge note, MRI report dated 2026-06-16, injection procedure note, clinic visit notes documenting exam findings and symptom duration, and letter of medical necessity from Dr. Lindqvist].

Because this appeal concerns a determination that clinical documentation was incomplete rather than a substantive clinical denial, I ask that MedStar Family Choice DC identify the specific InterQual or other criteria elements at issue, confirm receipt of the enclosed records, and issue a decision as promptly as possible given the patient's ongoing neurologic symptoms and functional limitation.

Please direct any questions or requests for additional information to me at [phone number] or [email address], or to Dr. Lindqvist's office at [practice phone/fax].

I understand from the denial notice that this appeal must be received by 2027-01-30. I am submitting this appeal well in advance of that date. I also note that MedStar Family Choice DC's publicly posted enrollee appeals process describes a 60-calendar-day appeal window from the date of the Adverse Benefit Determination notice, which differs from the 180-day deadline stated in the notice I received; I am filing promptly so that this appeal is timely under either standard, and I ask MedStar Family Choice DC to confirm in writing which deadline applies to this case.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Jordan Hayes
